```python
def count_rotation(arr):
    for i in range(1, len(arr)):
        if arr[i] < arr[i - 1]:
            return i
    return 0


assert count_rotation([3, 2, 1]) == 1
assert count_rotation([1, 2, 3]) == 0
assert count_rotation([3, 1, 2]) == 1
assert count_rotation([2, 3, 1]) == 2
assert count_rotation([4, 5, 1, 2, 3]) == 2
assert count_rotation([]) == 0
```

This scans from index 1 and returns the first index whose element is smaller than its predecessor, or 0 if there is none. For a rotated ascending array, that index is the position of the minimum, which is the number of rotations. It runs in O(n) time and O(1) extra space. For `[3, 2, 1]` the first descent is at index 1, so it returns 1, as your assert expects.
